role: @main entry of the watchOS app: holds the session manager and strap connector it takes from WatchDependencies.current as @StateObjects, reads the workout manager from its app delegate (WatchAppDelegate, which also hands a recovered workout session to it and wires the workout manager to the session manager, at a recovery relaunch or when the root view appears) and builds the WatchLiveView scene.
types: WatchApp: struct (App, @main) — Watch app entry; its services come from the Watch composition root, WatchDependencies, and its app delegate
WatchAppDelegate: class (NSObject, WKApplicationDelegate; MainActor by target default) — owns the WatchWorkoutManager and receives watchOS's active-workout recovery call
toplevel: Stored-property initializers read WatchDependencies.current.sessionManager and .strapConnector (the process-wide instances unless a substitute is set); the delegate adaptor creates WatchAppDelegate, whose stored initializer constructs the one WatchWorkoutManager. The file reads no `.shared` instance; WatchDependencies.swift is the Watch target's only root file in scripts/check_no_shared_outside_root.sh.

units.does: The workout manager the app delegate owns (appDelegate.workoutManager), passed to WatchLiveView and wired up in wireUp.

App init: reads WatchDependencies.current and attaches its session manager to its strap connector so direct-strap HR samples have a destination before any view exists. In the app these are WatchSessionManager.shared (first touch runs its init, activating WCSession) and WatchStrapConnector.shared.
units.entry: @main: SwiftUI instantiates WatchApp at process launch

units.does: Scene body: one WindowGroup showing WatchLiveView(sessionManager, workoutManager) with strapConnector injected as environment object; onAppear runs wireUp(), scenePhase changes go to followScenePhase, and displayOnlyMode changes (and the initial value) call strapConnector.setAutoReconnect(!displayOnly) so the wrist reconnects a saved strap only in legacy mode.

Scene phase change: .background → strapConnector.appDidEnterBackground() (ends any discovery scan); .active → sessionManager.requestCurrentStateFromPhone() (deduplicated with launch's in-flight pull).

branches.effect: false: return; true: pull current state

units.does: First-appear wiring: wires the workout manager to the session manager through the app delegate (WatchAppDelegate.wire: attach, starting the keep-alive session if already recording, and follow the phone's messages for silence detection; a no-op when a recovery relaunch already did it), requests HealthKit authorization in a Task, and pulls the current state from the iPhone.

Begins the recovery first (workoutManager.recoverActiveSession, so a recording state the session manager already holds makes a start that waits for it), then wires the workout manager to WatchDependencies.current.sessionManager at once (wire(to:)), since a background relaunch may never show the root view that otherwise wires it; the iPhone's messages, including the activation state pull's reply, then reach the workout manager.
units.entry: WKApplicationDelegate: watchOS calls it after relaunching the app to recover the workout session that was active when the app was ended.

units.does: Attaches the delegate's workout manager to `sessionManager` (WatchSessionManager.attach, which starts it when the iPhone is already recording) and makes it follow the session manager's messages (followPhoneMessages). Each keeps only its first call, so the recovery relaunch and WatchApp.wireUp can both run it.
